Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 86, verse 1:

Surah At-Tariq: An Overview

In the introduction to this part (juz') we stated that this surah consists of successive, intense blows upon the dormant human conscience, intense to the utmost degree, and of spontaneous cries of alarm, such as are raised to awaken a person who is sunk in the sleep of heedlessness. These blows and these spontaneous calls carry the following meaning: Arise, awake, look, pay attention, reflect, and use deep thought. After all, there is a Maker and Manager of this machinery of creation. Behind this universe a wise power is at work. This entire universe runs according to a fixed and orderly law. Look, your trial is taking place in this world. You are responsible for your words and deeds, and you will have to present the account of your whole life. A severe punishment is also prepared, and a blessed Paradise of great bounties is also present, which has a system like that of a great kingdom.

This surah is an example of these characteristics. Its blows are as intense as the scenes they describe. The musical style is also intense. The rhythm of its words is intense, and its meaningful indications are also intense. For instance, the words al-Tariq, al-Thaqib, al-Daafiq, al-Raj' and al-Sad' are intense in their wording, their meaning and their rhythm.

An example of intensity in meaning is that every soul is being watched over.

"In kullu nafsin lamma alayha hafiz" (86:4): "There is no soul over which there is not a guardian." And on the Day of Judgment the conditions will be so severe that no one will have any power of their own, nor any helper.

"Yawma tubla al-sara'ir..." (86:9-10): "On the Day when hidden secrets are examined, man will have no power of his own, nor any helper." And this is the final and decisive word of the Qur'an.

"Innahu la-qawlun fasl, wa ma huwa bil-hazl" (86:13-14): "It is a decisive word, and it is not a jest." Then, the threat given in this surah includes a manner of intensity and severity.

"Innahum yakiduna kaydan, wa akidu kaydan, fa-mhili al-kafirina amhilhum ruwayda" (86:15-17): "These people are devising schemes, and I too am devising a scheme. So leave the disbelievers alone, O Prophet, for a little while, and let them be given respite."

As we said in the introduction to this part, it contains all the themes: that this universe has a God, that this universe runs according to a plan and a decree, that this life is a trial, that man is responsible for his deeds and words, and that a day will come on which reward and punishment will take place, and so on.

There is complete harmony and correspondence between the cosmic scenes presented and the doctrinal purposes presented. Its detailed eloquence will become clear when we also discuss the verses of the Holy Qur'an. In terms of its manner of expression, the verses of the Qur'an possess unparalleled beauty.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 86, verses 2–3:

"And what will make you know what the Tariq is?" (86:2). It is as though it is a thing beyond the grasp of human understanding. After this, the Holy Qur'an itself defines and explains it: "It is the piercing star" (86:3). It is called thaqib (piercing) because, by its rays, it tears through the darkness and casts its light upon the earth. In this sense, every star is a piercing star. From this verse we cannot determine which star it is, nor is there any great need to specify it; rather, it is better to take it to mean stars in general. The meaning then becomes: "By the sky and by the shining stars within it, which tear through the darkness and bring light," and by that light they emerge, tearing through the veil of darkness that conceals other things. This meaning also points to the realities and concepts stated in the surah, as will come out in the explanation that follows.

The answer to the oath is: over every soul there is a guardian appointed by Allah, by His command.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 86, verse 4:

"There is no soul but that it has a guardian over it." The words and the construction in which this is stated are a strongly emphatic style. It is a negation and an affirmation: there is no soul except that a watcher has been appointed over it. He both watches over it and records its deeds, and this guardian also protects it, and his appointment is by the command of Allah. All these matters are attributed to the soul (nafs), because all human secrets and all human thoughts are within the human soul, and it is this soul that bears responsibility for reward and punishment.

The reality is that human beings have not been left aimlessly, like an unrestrained camel roaming wherever it wishes, with no protector or shepherd, and with no one left in the valleys of the earth without a watcher, so that they may wander wherever they like and graze wherever they like, with no one to ask them. Rather, the deeds of human beings are being recorded with great precision, and this record is being prepared directly for each person, and it is being done with complete exactness.

This verse brings forward the fearful reality that a person, however alone he may appear, is never alone at any time. When no one in the world is watching him, Allah and Allah's representative are watching and recording. If no worldly eye is seeing him, and not even the light of any star reaches him, Allah's gaze is upon him and Allah's appointed guardian is attached to him. This is just as the light of a shooting star pierces through darkness and reaches its target; likewise, no veil stands between a person and Allah's watch. And Allah's appointed guardian is attached to him, just as the light of a shooting star pierces through darkness and reaches its target. Likewise, no veil stands between a person and Allah's watch. And the works of Allah are uniform: just as they operate in the horizons, so they operate within the self (anfus).

Having awakened the sense of the human soul through this pinch, it is connected to the cosmos. Now, through another pinch, its awareness of Allah's profound planning and inescapable decree is awakened. The oath by the heavens and the stars pointed towards this profound planning. Now it is told that the human being, the earth and the stars are a matter of far lesser concern; even your own self is a wonder of divine power. The very creation of the human being shows that this human is not an unrestrained camel, nor is he self-growing, nor is he a purposeless sequence of existence and non-existence.

Human beings should reflect on what they were created from, and how they became what they are before their very eyes. He was created from a water that gushes forth and comes out of the human body. And where does it come from? It comes out from between a person's back and chest. This water gathers from the spinal bones of the man, and the woman's fluid comes out from the upper bones of her chest. The formation of this water and its emission in this way was one of the secrets of Allah that human beings did not yet know. In the last half century, science, in accordance with its own methods of research, has lifted the veil from some of its aspects, and it has been found that within the bones of the man's back and the upper bones of the woman's chest, the woman's fluid (manawiyyah, seminal fluid) is formed, and when these two substances come together in an extremely secure place, a human being is created from them.

The truth is that the journey from the first creation of a human being to his final form is a long and frightening one. The water that comes out between the spinal bones and the chest bones has a long journey to a complete human being with a form and shape, one who also possesses intellect. He also possesses a complex composition of organic, nervous, intellectual and psychological elements. This journey, in which a gushing water passes through stages and takes the form of an adult human being of sound mind, also shows that there is a power outside the human being that directs this liquid water in a certain direction, whereas in its initial state there is within this water neither power nor any form. This water traverses this long journey in an extremely wondrous manner and reaches its destination. From this it becomes clear that by the command of Allah a supervisor has been appointed over it, who watches over this minute point, within which there is no intellect and no visible form, no power and no will, and who remains a constant supervisor throughout this long journey of the point. Within this point there are so many wonders that a human being cannot see so many wonders and marvels from the beginning to the end of his conscious life.

This is an extremely minute point, which is barely visible even through a very powerful microscope. When this water gushes forth once from the man's back, within it there are tens of millions of such points, and one of them reaches its destination. The fact that this point has no shape, has no intellect, has no power, and has no will becomes evident at the time when this point comes to rest in the womb of the mother and then seeks nourishment. Now the hand of power guides it in such a way that this point begins to consume the walls of the womb around it, and it creates for itself a pool of blood within the womb. This blood serves as its food. As soon as it is assured that the arrangement for its sustenance has been made, it begins a new operation. Now it begins to divide, division upon division, and continues to divide constantly. This simple, mindless, shapeless, weak and powerless cell, deprived of power and will, knows what it has to do and in which direction to proceed. It is the hand of power that protects it, guides it, and endows it with power and will, so that it knows where it has to go and what form it has to take. The hand of power commands it to assign the cells produced by this process of constant division to the work for which they are being created. The cells produced for a particular part of this structure move toward that organ, whereas the structure of the human body as a whole is an extremely complex structure. The cells produced by the process of division move constantly and gather in the form of organs, and at last this great edifice is formed. These cells create the muscular system within the human body. Then a group of them forms the nervous system. A group of them spreads the network of arteries. These and the other complex systems of this structure are formed, but this process of construction and formation is not as simple as it is commonly thought to be. Within this system an extremely profound technology is at work. Among the bones, every bone; among the muscles, every single muscle; and among the nerves, every single fiber, is not fully similar or identical to any other bone or fiber. No muscle is identical to other nerves, because this structure is extremely complex. Its composition is also extremely strange. The function and duty of each is distinct. Therefore, every cell learns from the Teacher of power and understands for which particular organ it is destined, and what duty it has to perform within that organ. Therefore, within the body, even the smallest cell moves, and under the guidance of the Teacher of power it knows well its own path: where it has to go, what its duty is, and what it has to do. No single cell, nor any group of them, ever loses its way. For example, the cells that form the eye know that the eye is located in the head. It is not permissible for them to form eyes in the stomach, the feet, or the arms. Although, if Allah wills, He could make an eye in any place in the stomach, the hands or the feet. If the first cell that forms the eye were to go to those places and form an eye there, it could do so; but when the eye cell travels, it travels toward the very place that has been designated for it within this intricate human form. The question is: who gives these commands to this cell or these cells? Who is it that has decided that the eye should be in this place and should not be in that place? It is the Being of Allah, the Exalted. It is Allah alone, the Guardian and the Most High, who supervises these cells, gives them guidance, shows them the way, and guides them through darknesses where no one other than Allah could ever make a path.

All these cells, both collectively and individually, operate within the framework that the overall order of these cells establishes for them. Within this overall order there is the form of the organ and also hereditary characteristics. For example, if these are the cells of a human eye, they will form a human eye, and furthermore, within that eye will be preserved the particular shape and form of that person's ancestors. Even a slight deviation from this blueprint disturbs the system of that organ. So the question remains: who is that Being who gave the cells this power and taught them the method of performing such orderly work? Although it is a simple cell, and it has no intellect or perception, nor power and will. The straightforward answer to this question is that it is only the Being of Allah. It is Allah who teaches these cells what they know, such that a human being can neither draw such a blueprint, nor create an organ, nor a hand, nor an eye, nor any part of them. On the contrary, a simple cell or a collection of cells accomplishes this work, which is an extremely great and complex task.

Within this brief survey of the journey from a single cell to a human being, there is a world of wonders and marvels, that is, in the stages from gushing water to becoming a human being. The system of organs: we are unable even to describe the details of these wonders. Nor is it possible within the limited pages of Zilal al-Quran. But all these wonders are a clear witness that there is a hidden hand of power which makes these cells perform this work. From these realities, one truth is established, the truth on which Allah has sworn by the sky and by al-Tariq (the Piercing Star). This oath and its answer serve as an introduction to another great truth: that all human beings will, in the same way, rise again from their graves through a self-operating process. But the polytheists of Makkah, who were the first addressees of the Qur'an, and before whom this surah was first revealed, denied this second truth.

It is Allah who created man and then sustained him. Therefore He is able to give him life again after death, and to bring him back to new life after he has died and been mingled with the dust. The first creation, mentioned above, bears witness that He is able to bring him back to life. The first life is a witness of trustworthy testimony to Allah's providence and power, because the first creation contains a most wise technology. If the restoration of man to life and his being called to account is not accepted, then the entire system of the first creation would become purposeless.

On the Day when secrets are tested (86:9): the day when hidden mysteries will be examined. When concealed secrets are exposed, and the veils within whose folds these secrets lie are lifted, these secrets will be scrutinised; they will be manifest and open, and will no longer remain secrets. Just as a shining star emerges from the darkness, and just as the human self is wrapped within veils, with its guardian knowing its every word, so on the Day when man has neither strength nor any helper, everything will come to the fore.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 86, verse 10:

﴿فَمَا لَهُ مِن قُوَّةٍ وَلَا نَاصِرٍ﴾ (86:10) "At that time man will have neither his own strength nor anyone to help him." That is, there will be neither personal power nor any help coming from outside. Nothing will remain hidden, and all of a person's weaknesses will be exposed, so that will be an extremely severe moment. The awareness of such circumstances has a profound effect on a person: this universe, then the human self, then the various stages of human creation, and finally the helplessness of a person on the Day of Judgment, when all secrets will be revealed and all powers and supports will come to an end.

Perhaps some doubt still remains. Within the human self there is some disquiet, and at times a person still harbours doubts even after a most effective speech and irrefutable proofs. Therefore, after emphatic oaths, it is stated again that this is a decisive matter, and here too a connection is established between this Qur'an and the universe, just as was done at the beginning of the surah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 86, verses 11–14:

Al-raj' (ar-rajʿ) means "returning," and the sky sends rain again and again. Al-sadʿ (aṣ-ṣadʿ) means "splitting open." When, after rain, plants grow out of the earth, the earth splits and sprouts emerge from it. These two things express one kind of life: plants and their first life, in that water falls from the heavens and then plants grow. This image bears a closer resemblance to the water of the seed leaping forth and pouring out, and a child emerging from the darkness of the womb, coming from between the backbone and the breastbone rather than from the sky. It is as if there is one life and one scene, one kind of movement, one system and one kind of creation, and from both it is established that the Creator of both is one. No reasonable person can claim that he can create such a creation or produce creatures resembling these creations.

This scene is also similar to the scene of a shining star. The light of such a star also breaks through the veils of darkness and comes into view, and just as this light appears, so too will hidden secrets appear. Thus these scenes are also similar, and from them too the power of one Creator becomes known.

Are these two cosmic creatures that are being sworn by, or are they two cosmic events that are being sworn by: the sky that repeatedly sends rain, and the earth that repeatedly splits because of the growth of vegetation. The scene of these two events or occurrences, the hints hidden within that scene, and the certainty and firmness of the words raj' and sadʿ themselves, and then the oath of Allah along with them, prove that the resurrection and accountability are a definite matter. It is not a joke. Or, this entire Qur'an speaks a definite word, and nothing within it has been said merely for the sake of speaking. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 86, verses 15–16:

We have indeed made clear the reality of these people: they were created from a gushing fluid that issues from between the loins of the father and the breastbone of the mother. In its initial stage, that fluid had no power, no strength, and no will; neither knowledge nor guidance. The Hand of Divine Power brought these people into existence through this long process, and one day they will be created again in the same way, all their secrets will be revealed, and they will then be just as helpless and powerless as before. Are these people plotting against the movement of Allah? I am their Creator, their Guide, their Protector, the One who brings them into being, causes them to die, and returns them. I have placed them in this trial. I am All-Powerful and Irresistible, and I am the Creator of the twinkling stars in the heavens. From the water from which they were created, I made a human being who speaks and thinks. It is Allah who made this sky, which sends down rain and causes vegetation to grow from it. It is I who do this work, and I also counter their schemes with My own plans.

Now, on one side are the schemes of these people, and on the other side are the plans of Allah. The truth is that whatever happens is exactly what God wills. In this contest there is really only one party; the second party, which appears to be visible, is merely for the sake of mockery.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 86, verse 17:

فمھل ................ رویدا (17:86) "So leave, O Prophet, these disbelievers; grant them a little respite." Do not be hasty; the outcome of this confrontation is not far off. You have seen the reality of this confrontation. Even this small respite given to these people is granted under a great wisdom, and this respite is indeed brief, even if your whole life is spent in it, because the life that has been given to human beings for this world is, indeed, brief.

The manner of expression is full of affection. Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger that he should grant them respite.

فمھل…………رویدا (17:86) "Grant these disbelievers respite for a short time." As if the Prophet ﷺ holds the matter in his hands, as if granting respite is within his authority, whereas in reality the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has no authority over anything at all. This is a manner of affection. Through this manner the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the bearer of mercy and compassion, feels breezes of tenderness. His desire for immediate success is submerged in this atmosphere, and thus Allah merges His will with the will of His Messenger, and apparently it seems as though he were a partner in authority. Thus the veils are lifted from before him, and he reaches the station where definitive decisions are made. It is as if it is being said: these powers are in your hands, but you should grant a little respite. This is a manner of affection, an exceedingly subtle manner of intimacy and love. By such a manner of speech, all the hardships that were befalling you on this path are removed. All fatigue and all difficulties are dispelled; mountains of trials and hardships melt away, and the atmosphere is overshadowed by the shade of intimacy and love.
